take: US crude imports from Venezuela hit 701,000 b/d in July, the highest since 2017 before easing to 655,000 b/d in August, which matters because heavy sour barrels are exactly what US refiners need whilst they run above 95% utilisation and tilt yields towards middle distillates on fat jet and diesel margins. On the shipping side, the orderbook has grown three and a half times since 2020 against only 30% yard capacity growth, setting up a 2028 delivery crunch that will eventually loosen tanker and bulker supply but does nothing for prompt freight. The inventory angle is the distillate pull: refiners maximising middle distillate output after global crude runs fell 4.8 million b/d, or 6%, in 2Q26 means gasoil and jet stocks stay tight relative to gasoline, so watch product cracks rather than flat price for the real signal. Cross-market, the Capital Tankers 15-month suezmax fixture worth $73.1m to $82.2m and Venergy doubling its VLCC order at Hengli show owners still committing capital to tonne-miles even as the forward delivery wave builds. Iraq claiming output above 5 million b/d complicates its OPEC quota push and is the bearish supply tail risk to watch, alongside any Democratic-controlled Congress noise on Venezuelan oil deals.

items.summary: Global crude oil refinery inputs fell by 4.8 million barrels per day (b/d) in the second quarter of 2026 (2Q26), or 6%, following the start of conflict in late February in the Middle East, according to data from Kpler. items.title: U.S. refineries have been running at very high rates in 2026

Tight global product supplies this year have boosted margins for petroleum products, particularly for diesel, incentivizing the increased run rates.
